problem: Jacob has two email accounts, account $A$ and account $B.$ In account $A$ he receives $40%$ of his emails and he receives the remaining $60%$ in account $B.$ Approximately $30%$ of the emails received in account $A$ are spam and $36%$ of the emails received in both accounts are spam. What is the probability that a randomly selected email from account $B$ is spam? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
worked_solution:
Let $S$ be the event that the chosen email is spam, and let $A$ be the event that the email selected is from account $A.$ Then ${A}^{′}$ is the event that the email selected is from account $B.$

To calculate the probability that a randomly selected email is spam, we can use the law of total probability:

$$
P(S)=P(S|A)P(A)+P(S|{A}^{′})P({A}^{′})
$$

Let's go through the problem statement and translate each bit of information into mathematical notation.

- Since $40%$ of the emails are received in account $A$ and the remaining $60%$ in account $B,$ we have

$$
P(A)=0.40,\,P({A}^{′})=0.60.
$$

- Since $30%$ of the emails received in account $A$ are spam, we have 

$$
P(S|A)=0.30.
$$

- Since $36%$ of the emails received in both accounts are spam, we have 

$$
P(S)=0.36.
$$

Substituting the above information into the law of total probability and solving for $P(S|{A}^{′})$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(S) & =P(S|A)P(A)+P(S|{A}^{′})P({A}^{′}) \\ 0.36 & =(0.30)(0.40)+P(S|{A}^{′})(0.60) \\ 0.36 & =0.12+0.6P(S|{A}^{′}) \\ 0.6P(S|{A}^{′}) & =0.24 \\ P(S|{A}^{′}) & =0.40.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that a randomly selected email from account $B$ is spam is $0.40.$
